{{Short description|French mathematician (born 1979)}}
'''Sébastien Gouëzel''' (born November 20, 1979) is a French mathematician and a research director at the [[CNRS]] (French National Centre for Scientific Research). He is known for his contributions to [[dynamical system]]s, [[ergodic theory]], [[probability theory]], and formal mathematics.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://perso.univ-rennes1.fr/sebastien.gouezel/ |title=Sébastien Gouëzel - Personal webpage |access-date=2024-12-19}}</ref>

== Education and career ==

Gouëzel was educated at the [[École normale supérieure]] in Paris from 1998 to 2002. In 2000, he achieved first place in the [[Agrégation]] in mathematics. He completed his DEA (master's degree) in pure mathematics at the [[University of Paris-Sud]] in 2001 with highest honors, ranking first in his class. His master's thesis, supervised by [[Viviane Baladi]], was titled "Spectrum of the transfer operator in dimension 1."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://perso.univ-rennes1.fr/sebastien.gouezel/ |title=Curriculum Vitae - Sébastien Gouëzel |access-date=2024-12-19}}</ref>

He earned his PhD in mathematics in 2004 under the supervision of Viviane Baladi, with a dissertation titled "Decorrelation speed and limit theorems for non-uniformly expanding maps."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://perso.univ-rennes1.fr/sebastien.gouezel/ |title=Curriculum Vitae - Sébastien Gouëzel |access-date=2024-12-19}}</ref>

Gouëzel's academic positions include:
* 2002–2005: ''Agrégé préparateur'' at [[École normale supérieure]] Paris
* 2005–2009: Research associate (second class) at CNRS, [[University of Rennes]]
* 2009–2015: Research associate (first class) at CNRS, University of Rennes
* 2015–2020: Research director (second class) at CNRS, [[University of Nantes]]
* 2020–2021: Research director (second class) at CNRS, University of Rennes
* 2021–present: Research director (first class) at CNRS, University of Rennes<ref>{{cite web |url=https://perso.univ-rennes1.fr/sebastien.gouezel/ |title=Curriculum Vitae - Sébastien Gouëzel |access-date=2024-12-19}}</ref>

== Research ==

Gouëzel's research spans several areas of mathematics, with particular focus on:

=== Dynamical Systems and Ergodic Theory ===
His work includes significant contributions to the study of [[hyperbolic dynamical system]]s, transfer operators, and [[central limit theorem|limit theorems]] for dynamical systems. Notable results include work on the [[Teichmüller space|Teichmüller flow]] and spectral properties of various dynamical systems.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Avila |first1=Artur |last2=Gouëzel |first2=Sébastien |last3=Yoccoz |first3=Jean-Christophe |title=Exponential mixing for the Teichmüller flow |journal=Publications mathématiques de l'IHÉS |volume=104 |pages=143–211 |year=2006 |doi=10.1007/s10240-006-0001-5}}</ref>

=== Random Walks on Groups ===
Gouëzel has made important contributions to the theory of [[random walk]]s on [[hyperbolic group]]s, including work on [[Martin boundary]] theory and local limit theorems.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Gouëzel |first=Sébastien |title=Local limit theorem for symmetric random walks in Gromov-hyperbolic groups |journal=Journal of the AMS |volume=27 |pages=893–928 |year=2014 |issue=3 |doi=10.1090/S0894-0347-2014-00788-8|arxiv=1209.3217 }}</ref>

=== Formal Mathematics ===
He is a major contributor to the [[Lean (proof assistant)|Lean theorem prover]] and maintains the mathematical library mathlib. His formalization work includes differential geometry, the [[Gromov–Hausdorff convergence|Gromov-Hausdorff distance]], and various results in ergodic theory.<ref>{{cite conference |last=Gouëzel |first=Sébastien |title=A formalization of the change of variables formula for integrals in mathlib |conference=CICM 2022 |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |volume=13467 |pages=3–18 |year=2022 |doi=10.1007/978-3-031-16681-5_1}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==

* 2018: Invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Rio de Janeiro<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm/icm-2018/invited-speakers |title=ICM 2018 Invited Speakers |publisher=International Mathematical Union |access-date=2024-12-19}}</ref>
* 2019: [[Michael Brin Prize in Dynamical Systems]] for his outstanding contributions to dynamical systems, ergodic theory, and geometric group theory<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www.aimsciences.org/article/doi/10.3934/jmd.2020015 |title=The 2019 Michael Brin Prize in Dynamical Systems |journal=Journal of Modern Dynamics |year=2020 |doi=10.3934/jmd.2020015 |access-date=2024-12-19}}</ref>
* 2022: [[:fr:Prix Madame-Victor-Noury|Grand Prix Madame Victor Noury]] from the [[French Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/en/node/1725 |title=Grand Prix Madame Victor Noury 2022 |publisher=French Academy of Sciences |access-date=2024-12-19}}</ref>
